thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Dedicated pool 'merchantprime-dp' (tenant=MerchantPrime) reporting sustained GPU utilization 96-99% and request queueing for 7m. latency p95 -> 3.2s (baseline 0.7s). auto-scale did not trigger. paging ops-oncall and eng-sre.

mika: taking this. oncall-assign -> mika (eng-sre). I'll gather quick metrics and propagate. :pager:

alex: looking now. seeing steady queue depth growth on the tenant shard. top signs are long-running token-generation jobs from a single API key. suspect a runaway workload. pulling pod list.

alex: snippets from metrics:
```
merchantprime-dp GPU util: 96.8%
active_infer_reqs: 124 -> 180 (growth)
avg_latency_token_ms: 12.6
queue_depth_by_tenant: {MerchantPrime: 172}
```

ops-oncall: confirmed alert and handoff to me. I've locked paging channel and started the dedicated-pool playbook: https://redwood.playbooks/run/dedicated-gpu-pressure

priya: I'm on the account side. MerchantPrime CS reached out mentioning 'slow responses for production customers'. They've warned of potential SLA violation. Any immediate mitigation that doesn't require engineering on their side?

mika: short-term options:
- approve temporary burst (manual reserve add) of +4 GPUs to merchantprime-dp (affects capacity costs)
- isolate tenant: throttle MerchantPrime traffic at ingress (rate-limit) until load subsides
- evict/kill long-running low-priority jobs from tenant (if allowed)

alex: autoscaler didn't kick because the tenant is pinned to a fixed cap in their Dedicated config (commit limits). It will require manual reserve or eviction. We can also failover some incoming requests to the hosted fallback model (lower-cost variant) for non-critical routes via routing policy.

ops-oncall: action checklist:
1) Contact infra to approve temporary burst? @finance? (cost ok for now, need AM signoff)
2) Apply emergency rate-limit on tenant token at edge
3) Start eviction of oldest requests >5m

emily: ops-team can approve a 30-minute burst of +6 GPUs to merchantprime-dp to relieve queue. Need explicit approval from Priya / account owner to bill. Priya, can you confirm?

priya: I got MerchantPrime on the phone. They want us to keep service up. Approve the burst for 30m. They'll accept cost overage for the window. Please ensure we notify them when we scale down. :white_check_mark:

juan: I'll run the burst command now and apply emergency ingress rate-limit of 100 rps for non-priority endpoints.

juan: commands executed:
```
# temporary bump
infractl dedicated reserve add --pool merchantprime-dp --gpus 6 --duration 30m --reason "emergency burst approved by AM"
# ingress rate-limit
edgectl rate-limit set --tenant MerchantPrime --limit 100
```

alex: seeing immediate drop in queue depth and p95 latency falling.
```
after_bump GPU util: 72.3%
queue_depth: 32
p95 latency: 0.9s
```

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation applied (burst +6GPUs, ingress throttle). No data plane errors observed. Marking page severity -> reduced. Please continue monitoring for 60m.

mika: continuing watch. action items: follow up on root cause (why autoscaler didn't trigger given pinned cap), add guardrail to detect single-tenant floods, propose auto-eviction policy for non-critical jobs.

priya: I'll send a customer update: brief recap, we applied temporary capacity and set rate limits, will follow up with a postmortem and cost reconciliation.

emily: creating a short incident record and will schedule a follow-up postmortem tomorrow with product, infra, and account team. Owner: mika.

ops-oncall: adding immediate TODOs:
- [mika] postmortem and new alert: autoscaler-failure-on-pinned-pool
- [alex] implement per-tenant runaway-detection metric and alert
- [infra] review burst policy UX for quicker approvals
- [priya] customer communication + invoice note

juan: rolling scale-down in 25m unless queue starts rising again. Notifying merchantprime slack contact when scale-down begins.

mika: taking ownership for the postmortem. will include timeline, metrics, and remediation plan. closing live mitigation. :lock_with_ink_pen:

ops-oncall: closing page, reassigning to mika for post-incident follow-up. If anyone sees regressions ping this thread.

priya: thanks everyone. MerchantPrime confirmed improved responsiveness and appreciated the quick action.
